https://yle.fi/a/74-20246138.text: Former Finnish Prime Minister Sanna Marin and Social Democratic Party leader Antti Lindtman had just passed through a Ukrainian railway station when it was targeted by a Russian drone strike on Sunday. Marin, Lindtman and Tuulia Pitkänen , Marin's former aide, had been attending the same security conference as several former political leaders and security advisers. A Russian drone struck a separate train's engine near the Ukraine-Poland border on Sunday. No casualties were reported. Shortly before the attack, a train carrying the Finnish delegation as well as senior figures including former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson passed through the station. "The news certainly gave us pause," Lindtman told Yle in a text message. He said the absence of casualties was most likely due to Ukrainians having learned how to prepare for such attacks. "Russia is becoming more aggressive and more ruthless by the day, and its strikes are getting ever closer to Europe's borders," Prime Minister Petteri Orpo (NCP) said, commenting on the strike. "They are playing a very dangerous game." The train that was hit was travelling from Kyiv to Warsaw. Russia carried out a series of strikes across Ukraine on Sunday, with one attack reportedly landing just 800 metres from the Polish border, according to news agency AFP.
